title: Learned Meta-Tokens for Language Modeling
claim: Models trained with injected meta-tokens and meta-attention retain high accuracy on long inputs where standard baselines fail, especially with limited training length.
layout: 2 side-by-side grouped bar charts, shared legend style, value labels atop bars
description: Two grouped bar charts sit side by side. The left is titled 'Accuracy at Eval Length = 512 on Parity' and the right 'Accuracy at Eval Length = 512 on Copying'. Each chart has four model groups on the x-axis: GPT-2 APE, Meta + APE, Meta + RoPE and GPT-Neo-125M. Within each group, red, orange and blue bars show train lengths 128, 256 and 512. Exact accuracy values are printed above the bars. The y-axis is accuracy in percent, from 0 to 100. The Meta groups reach about 96-100% on parity. On copying they reach 98-99% at the longest train length. GPT-2 APE stays low, at 53-61% on parity and under 8% on copying. GPT-Neo-125M has only a blue bar, at 54.8% on parity and 16.9% on copying. The eye goes first to the tall Meta bars, which stand out against the short baseline bars.
caption: We study the performance of the pre-trained GPT-2 w/ APE, Meta-attention w/ APE, and Meta-attention w/ RoPE, as well as GPT-Neo-125M, all fine-tuned on synthetic data for their respective tasks at the maximum train lengths indicated in the legends. All experiments are performed on a test set of prompt lengths up to 512 tokens.
abstract: Transformer-based language models (LMs) notably struggle to reliably capture distant contextual information. This work introduces a novel approach using meta-tokens -- special tokens injected during pre-training -- paired with a dedicated meta-attention mechanism to guide LMs to use these tokens. We pre-train a language model equipped with meta-attention in addition to causal multi-head attention on <100B tokens, achieving strong performance on a suite of synthetic tasks. Our method facilitates length generalization up to 2$\times$ the context window after extension with YaRN. We provide an information-theoretic analysis which reveals that meta-tokens \textit{sharpen} the positional encoding, allowing them to operate as content-based anchors that compress preceding context and “cache” it within the meta-token. We empirically confirm this by visualizing model internals to study the residual stream. Together, our findings demonstrate that meta-tokens and meta-attention provide a simple, data-efficient pre-training method, grounded by new mechanistic insights into their role in enabling length generalization behavior.
